reviews.text: Yan’s contribution to the franchise is innovative, subversive and entertaining.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: To sum up Birds Of Prey is a more than serviceable film. The performances of Margot Robbie and Ewan McGregor do allow the film to occasionally have an edge to it.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: This is without a doubt one of the must-see films of the year that is filled to the brim with stylish and superb filmmaking, thrilling action, engaging characters as well as a brilliantly catchy soundtrack.
reviews.author: Yasmine Kandil

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is about a lot more than being a colorful, fun action film–and it is a lot of that, too. This story is themed around sisterhood, identity, and finding independence.
reviews.author: Erica Richards

reviews.text: Where her beau has settled for becoming an icon for impotent white rage, BIRDS OF PREY breathes new life in a franchise running on empty.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Narrative wrinkles like these are hardly a deterrent when the rest of the film is so damn entertaining.
reviews.author: Mihir Fadnavis

reviews.text: From start to finish, Birds of Prey is a wild ride through the criminal underbelly of Gotham, filled with charming performances from the entire cast. It’s a shining star that justifies the popularity of the genre.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: With a phenomenal cast led by an outstanding Margot Robbie as Harley Quinn, Cathy Yan delivers some of the best action of the entire cinematic universe in a genuinely entertaining superhero flick.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The movie is so badly written and so entrenched in its own space that it manages the impossible: to make us dislike Margot Robbie in a character we've previously liked in a previous installment. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: This film is made to make you laugh as much as it’s made to entertain.
reviews.author: Mark Trujillo

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a female directed, written, and produced action flick. It’s something anyone old enough to see an R-rated movie can enjoy...
reviews.author: Kate Boyle

reviews.text: Next to [2004's] Catwoman, this the most egregious example among superhero films of filmmakers warping established characters to suit their own tastes and ideas rather than giving fans what they want to pay for.
reviews.author: Jonathan Garcia

reviews.text: There's this thing about bad vs. badder that does not help the stakes around anti-heroes or villains movies. This film is a mix of a lot of stuff that separated could've worked, but together is just incoherence. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: Abandons the “Why so serious?” tone of its [DCEU] predecessors and instead screams “Let’s put a smile on that face!”
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: It’s a flocking good time.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: It’s a female-led action-comedy directed by a woman, written by a woman, and essentially about getting on in life without a man. Together those things are an overdue breath of fresh air. But they don’t automatically make for a good movie.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is not just a fun film but one of substance and depth.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Birds of Prey employs many of the same visual tricks as Suicide Squad, such as cartoony onscreen titles to introduce its characters, but Yan has more control over her film than Ayer did over his.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Joker showed that DC is not afraid to take risks. Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of Harley Quinn) continues that trend and pushes more boundaries.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Outstanding fight scenes, well-crafted characters, and a team of powerful women are at the center of a movie that's both written and directed even better than I hoped it might be. This twisted story, told by one Harley Quinn, is a must-watch.
reviews.author: Zofia Wijaszka

reviews.text: A riot of good time entertainment, full of pop and fizz and punches to the nuts
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: With this film, "Bombshell", and "I, Tonya", Robbie is proving to be one of the most versatile actresses of our time.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: [This] is pretty refreshing for a film that could have just as easily settled for extending a comic-book brand with a bit of toothless corporate feminism.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: A fun, stylish, and female-empowering comic book adaptation. I loved the colorful atmosphere, fight choreography, and costumes! But it's the details acknowledging the female existence that stays with me.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Amid the movie's fun, if at times ham-handed girl power moments, and artfully choreographed fight scenes, this scene stands out for its serious-minded and affecting portrayal of sexual harassment.
reviews.author: Gabrielle Bruney

reviews.text: Kinetic, silly, candy-colored, and hyperviolent, Birds of Prey is a serious treat for fans of comic book films. But it wouldn't work without the equal parts goofy, hilarious, and unhinged performance of its lead.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: It's all frivolous fun sprinkled with a recurring theme of female independence that seems well ahead of its time.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Between its outrageous characters and fantastic final act, there is plenty for fans to love from this colorfully rambunctious joy ride.
reviews.author: Matthew Schuchman

reviews.text: Ultimately, the plot is as messy as its central character, trotting around with one shoe and a bacon sandwich in hand, but it's also a whole bunch of glittery, satisfying fun -- especially the unkempt, cheerful, chaotic energy of Harley Quinn.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Are there issues that could have been fixed to make this movie even better? Yes, but it's enough to make me want to see more of these characters, makes me want to see more films, and I can't wait to see what they do at how they expand this universe.
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a fruity cocktail of a movie. It goes down smooth, makes you giddy, and there's the possibility of a slight hangover.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: The movie is delightfully odd but not consistently inspired, often straining to rewrite the rules of superhero cinema, a mixture of good and bad ideas all mashed together.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Robbie has a gleeful, cheeky commitment to the character that sets the tone for the movie's 80s new wave kaleidoscopic aesthetic.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Yan takes the movie's visual scheme further by making it more explicitly a part of Harley's character and psychology.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Birds of Prey's narrative shortcomings are outweighed by its confidence and bombastic action, including a pitch-perfect performance from Margot Robbie as Harley Quinn.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: If Robbie explores more films like this, she could have a legit future as an action superstar. (pub. date Feb 2020)
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Quinn is simultaneously self-aware and oblivious, smart and ditzy, weak for a man and empowered by their split. The film rests on her dichotomy.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: The director brings the kinetic and chaotic energy demanded by Quinn and delivers an action film that thumps.
reviews.author: Brad Gullickson

reviews.text: Yan delivers above expectations. The action sequences are intricately staged with a continual surge of energy, movement and brutality.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: This fantabulous emancipation is a feminist tour de force with strong performances, a visually daring design, and a lot of fun, butt-kicking action.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a balancing act that includes pizazz, a reignited love for Harley Quinn, and a thirst to see where new ones can go.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Let's get this out of the way upfront, first and foremost, and most importantly, Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn) is dump trucks full of fun. It's almost as much fun as a dozen Golden Lab puppies.
reviews.author: Robert Slack

reviews.text: For a film that swings for the fences with its use of filmmaking techniques such as an animated opening sequence used to tell Harley's backstory, Birds of Prey is clearly a strong acting showcase.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: This is not to say that Birds of Prey isn't fun. It's a wild ride! Darkly comic and colorful, and the action is engaging without being too over-the-top (you know how superhero movies can get).
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: An acidic, technicolour demolition derby that shows what we can all achieve when we acknowledge that Gotham exists in more colours than simply black.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: It can be excessively fun and it can be excessively icky, but it never successfully marries the two.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: With a frenetic Kill Bill energy, Birds of Prey never takes itself too seriously... mostly the movie embraces the glorious absurdity of these camp characters a la Tim Burton's Batman Returns.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: I find Margot Robbie's performance disposable as the clown's carefree, volatile girlfriend. It is a dull, predictable and empty movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Directed with enough style and panache with well done action to be entertaining
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Whacky, zany, irreverant, bombastic and totally over-the-top.... An absolute visual feast... A tonne of balls-to-the-wall, goofy fun... unashamedly a really good time... It is a joy, a delight, and a blast from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: Birds of Prey sets the bar for nuanced depictions of female comic-book characters on the big screen...
reviews.author: Rebecca Long

reviews.text: But the best thing about 'Birds of Prey' (and its biggest draw) really is getting to see Harley Quinn shine in the spotlight for once and reclaim her own identity outside of the Joker.
reviews.author: Raffy Ermac

reviews.text: Although it tries very hard to capture the type of irreverent adult humor that the first Deadpool movie had, Birds of Prey is really just a female-led diamond heist movie. We already had Ocean's 8, thank you very much.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Cathy Yan's film is an intoxicating fun-filled cinematic experience. It'll leave you needing a cigarette and craving a perfectly made breakfast sandwich afterwards.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It's always one step away from being amazing, but the other steps they take are pretty entertaining.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: In a genre that busts out dozens of near-identical movies, superhero stories need more than visuals to be memorable.
reviews.author: Nikki Francisco

reviews.text: Robbie is still an exceptional casting decision; despite the flimsiness of Harley Quinn's character and scripting, Robbie looks and acts the part to considerable success.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: There may not be too many surprises, but Yan has announced herself as a creative force to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: A wild and wacky, candy-coated, glitter-filled grimy ride through the streets of Gotham with the motliest crew of characters as we explore themes of camaraderie, partnership, and female empowerment.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Robbie's Harley Quinn is best deployed in small doses. By placing her front and centre, in a film that teases a more communal feminine interest, her unceasing penchant for the overzealous quickly becomes exhausting.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: This is right here, bizarre, bonkers, bloody and brutal fun.
reviews.author: Andrew F. Peirce

reviews.text: Sputters to the finish line with its disjointed pacing, it's a damn good time with some dazzling fight scenes, dark humor, and a banner turn by Robbie.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: The cast is mostly spot-on, with Margot Robbie steals most of the show with her gleefully unhinged performance as Harley Quinn.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The movie has the DNA of Deadpool, and Scott Pilgrim vs The World, combined into the mutated one-of-a-kind masterpiece that is Birds of Prey.
reviews.author: Damian Levy

reviews.text: It blows up our notions of what makes a female superhero picture. It's antic and sure-of-itself and fabulously frenetic.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: To quote Harley Quinn herself, "Behind every successful man is a badass broad." In Birds of Prey, we find out she's even more badass when she steps out of his shadow.
reviews.author: Brooke Daugherty

reviews.text: [Robbie's] work here is fantastic, and perhaps comes the closest to the auteur-emphasized goals that Warner Bros. laid out for the DC films after the DCEU's collapse. Hopefully the trend continues.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: A raucous, deeply strange piece of punk-rock pop-art that's probably as close as anyone has come to making a Takeshi Miike or Sion Sono movie (or a Troma flick, for that matter) on a studio budget in years.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: The running gag in the film that all the violence and bloodshed is part of Harley's "emancipation" from her failed relationship with the Joker. It's the equivalent of those movies in which a middle-aged divorcee goes out and rediscovers life.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: It's just fun: it is raucous, it is intense, it is hard hitting, it is energetic, it is colorful, it is a dang good time at the movies.
reviews.author: Vera Wylde

reviews.text: If you happen to enjoy the animated Harley Quinn series on the DC Universe streaming platform, then this movie will be right up your alley. And even though this may not be saying much, this was better than Suicide Squad too.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Harley Quinn's first adventure as a headliner is among the DC Extended Universe's finest movies so far, and didn't need the shadow of the Bat looming over it any more than it needed Joker.
reviews.author: Sean Keane

reviews.text: What Yan and Hodson accomplish with Birds of Prey is the balance that's sometimes lacking in comic book films: They fulfill both the demands of the story and the demands of the characters.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: ...an often prototypically ineffective comic-book adaptation.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The hyper-active, chaotic comic book movie I didn't know that I wanted. The cherry on top is the top notch practical stunt work and fights.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: This super violent film has such an atrocious screenplay that I laughed when it was serious and was annoyed when it attempted humor. Why do some women filmmakers think the only way to be successful is to imitate guys? What a wasted opportunity.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: In 2020 the tired comic book movie genre needs something wired like "Birds of Prey." It's a crude carnival ride; violent, colourful, with subtle and not so subtle elevated empowerment moments.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: An excessive, frazzled tale of hyper-violence that plays out like Tom & Jerry in the colourful and hazardous world of Gotham City
reviews.author: Simon Weaving

reviews.text: The characters were good, and can actually get you into this film...a pretty dope movie, I'm happy I sat down and watched it.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: This is a fun movie, one of my favorite D.C. movies...I was shocked by just how much fun this was, having known nothing about it...this is really an R-rated Batman, a D.C. Deadpool. Margot Robbie is hilarious with such range...
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Harley Quinn really finds her feet and moves on from the Joker, and from Suicide Squad, and she is stronger and better for it. It's just a shame that she takes so long to get there.
reviews.author: Matt Looker

reviews.text: Although "Birds of Prey" suffers from an identity issue... the fantabulous highs far outweigh the middling lows...
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: I'm ready for the sequel.
reviews.author: Molly Templeton

reviews.text: "Birds of Prey" isn't just female-fronted, it's actually diverse... Even if the story is rather thin, you'll want to keep coming back to it, if only because it might just have one of 2020's best movie moments.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Bursting with feminine fury and more than a few great moments, Birds of Prey, whilst lacking on story, is a fun romp that allows Harley Quinn a platform to shine again.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Instead of focusing on the toxic masculinity of male superheroes, Birds of Prey allows women to be in the spotlight without the shackle a male presence.
reviews.author: Yasmin Kleinbart

reviews.text: starts off with great gusto and energy, literally willing us to get onboard with its maniacal take comic book antiheroism before becoming something decidedly more conventional-and even a bit sentimental
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: An extremely rough, clunky script hinders what should have been a much better movie, though the movie is fun enough to overcome some of the needless hurdles.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a sizable improvement over Suicide Squad but lacks a foolproof plan.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: An improvement over Suicide Squad in every respect, and this time the ending is the best part and not the worst
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Action-cinema cheesecake that makes one Harley Quinn, played by one Margot Robbie with all the colorfully explosive force of fireworks shoved up an exhaust pipe, the star of her own show.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: The various threads, however, don't come together as seamlessly as you'd hope; a better script and more focused direction would have significantly helped.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Better than Suicide Squad...but not that much better.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Despite the R-rating and the large body count of this action film, it is emotionally light in nature. The action is comic, rather than serious, the opposite of Christopher Nolan's Batman trilogy with its dark, tortured characters.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: It's a wonderful reversal that the latest out-of-left-field Batman spinoff Birds of Prey does much of what Joker was trying to do, but better and with more bite.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It's a real shame that, what could have been a great opportunity for Warner to completely stand out within the competition and shine with its own light winds up being more innocuous. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is unapologetic, chockers with talent, and full of witty criticisms of misogyny...
reviews.author: Merryana Salem

reviews.text: In the end, Birds of Prey feels very much like Oceans 8-it's a sincerely enjoyable film that largely operates at an above-average level of entertainment with a few sparks of genuine brilliance in between
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: Margot has proven herself in the past as a reliable actor but her shallow, psychopathic Betty Boop grates very early in the proceedings.
reviews.author: Paul Farren

reviews.text: The mind-bending color, creative urban details, stunning costumes, and frenetic energy create a dizzying spectacle -- and there's a heart-pounding soundtrack to boot.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: One of Robbie's strengths is her ability to fully immerse herself in any role and Harley is a character Robbie clearly relishes. It is a bravura performance -- a wild and wacky one which Robbie tackles with infectious enthusiasm.
reviews.author: Paula Fleri-Soler

reviews.text: In the end, Birds of Prey is a little too fast, busy, and loud to entirely work, but it has a bright energy, a great sense of humour, and genuinely likeable characters.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: It's not about stopping a blue beam that's shooting into the sky. Instead, it's about a group of very different women learning to value each other while kicking a lot of tail along the way.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: The punky fun of Birds of Prey is hard to deny.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Robbie is the No. 1 Australian movie star right now. I would watch her in anything...
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: The plot structure's just kind of insane.
reviews.author: Jaby Koay

reviews.text: I wanted to know more about the other female characters.
reviews.author: Achara Kirk

reviews.text: Margot Robbie's Harley Quinn was the best part of "Suicide Squad". In a Harley Quinn standalone movie she is not a box office draw. A waste of my time and their talent
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: What follows is a gleefully ruthless, visually bombastic treat, utilizing Robbie's chameleonic talents alongside a pleasingly game cast to create something really quite spectacular.
reviews.author: Tom Augustine

reviews.text: The journey of Harley from henchwoman to antagonist, and her determination to get out from under the shadow of her more famous boyfriend, is where the energies of the all-woman creative team have been directed.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: The directing and acting do manage to find some gold here and there. It's worth a watch, although most will probably wait for the rental price.
reviews.author: Callum Forbes

reviews.text: Under the film's hyper-formatted style and impersonal action, there's a pretty good movie straining to break out-which makes the waste of its creators' earnest exertions all the more dismaying.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: 'Birds of Prey' soars with violent female empowerment.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: I know why the caged nerd sings.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Kinetic superhero saga, serving as a showcase for Margot Robbie.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: There's some good wallpaper here and there, but its aesthetics still fail to coalesce enough to ever generate an appealing, involving world.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: [Margot Robbie] herself is fantastic. The action choreography is pretty good... If I have a quibble: it has probably the worst needle drops of any movie in recent history.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Full of style, personality, humor, and a killer ensemble cast, Birds of Prey is one of the most enjoyable DC films ever made.
reviews.author: Drew Dietsch

reviews.text: Bursting with personality, Birds of Prey and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn is easy to enjoy, but can't make itself out to be more than what it already is: a messily empowering Rated-R runaway train.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: If you want an intensive Superhero film with a timeline and overarching stories, massive fighting scenes, and world-ending villains, you might want to wait until Birds of Prey is out of the cinema.
reviews.author: Luther de Lange

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is an uneven yet entertaining offering that still does enough to ensure that Quinn gets another chance to shine. The cinematic comic book world feels richer for having her anarchic spirit in it.
reviews.author: Rob Carnevale

reviews.text: Harley Quinn: Birds of Prey (yes, I am going to keep using that title) is a fast, frenetic and fun movie with great action set pieces, a great soundtrack and you may never see your local takeaway shop in the same way even again.
reviews.author: Joel Fisher

reviews.text: Wanna see a film that lives, breathes and simply rocks its comic-book roots? Then take the crazy, colorful ride with this souped-up 'Harley' gal.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Birds Of Prey feels like posturing - woke for woke sake. It's cynical and insincere as well as weak filmmaking.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Birds of Prey provides another opportunity for Margot Robbie to showcase her talents and, for the most part, audiences will enjoy seeing the bipolar Harley Quinn create mayhem and carnage.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Does the positive energy of a female-centric comic book movie-made by women-compensate for the nihilistic, super-violent nature of its content? Is this really a step forward for women, behind the camera and in the audience? That's the conundrum presented
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Even if Birds of Prey doesn't reinvent the wheel, it sure as hell gets it spinning.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: If you want to understand the essence of women under patriarchy, in its starkest, funniest, and most extreme, see Birds of Prey, and emancipate the Harley within.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: "Birds" never takes flight.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Robbie taps into her inner psycho and delivers several stand-up-and-cheer moments for Harley Quinn fans everywhere. That's perfect for a 20-minute montage on YouTube.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: Enough of it is dazzling to draw attention away from how sluggishly the plot develops prior to the big showdown.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Birds of Prey emancipate itself from its predecessors, and exceeds them in every way. With a new director in Cathy Yan, and a new feminist vision, it makes a splash as a standalone film but gives hope for the future of DC and other comic book movies.
reviews.author: Adriana Gomez-Weston

reviews.text: Margot Robbie once again brings her all to the role of Dr. Harleen Quinzel and provides more layers to her character adding to her excellent performance in Suicide Squad. This film gives the audience what it promised.... The emancipation of Harley Quinn!!!!
reviews.author: Benjamin Gummery

reviews.text: Though it hides its sneer behind a half-arsed feminist agenda, Birds Of Prey is messy, lazy and needlessly unpleasant.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: This spinoff is definitely an improvement on its predecessor -- a film that opens the door to a lot of fun possibilities for Harley Quinn and her new partners in crime.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Call it upcycled, repurposed or just plain ripped-off, but it's made out of familiar and gaudy stuff.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: Hyper-violent cartoon fluff, with nary a moral in sight, unless you count keeping a hyena in a tiny New York apartment as an act of kindness. Maybe it was a rescue hyena? Whatever. Prepubescent girls sneaking a peek at pajama parties will be damaged.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: I gotta say, though, that for as long as they've been waiting, women deserve better than middling, pandering stuff like Captain Marvel and now Birds Of Prey.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: It's kind of a blast, and its themes of solidarity feel surprisingly genuine.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Director Cathy Yan (Dead Pigs, 2018) knows how to use the broken character as a narrative tool very well, and finally, gives Harley Quinn the movie she deserves. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The aspects that make the film entertaining are not solely reduced to Quinn's central protagonist, but in [director Cathy] Yan's style, in collaboration with [cinematographer] Matthew Libatique. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: Unlike David Ayer's 'Suicide Squad', it feels chaotic and messy on purpose. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: A movie that never really flies and relies 100% on Harley Quinn's antics instead of character development or plot. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Ocadiz

reviews.text: Much like Ms Quinn's favorite bite, an egg sandwich, Yan's film is big, cheesy, a little messy at times and encompasses a little too much fat, but it's also delicious and bursting with colour.
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: Harley wrestles with responsibility, toys with self-destruction, and gets backed into female solidarity. Antics lead to agency.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: Uncommonly sturdy fare for the DCEU, Birds of Prey is a surprisingly successful marriage of free-wheeling tone, razor-sharp style, and well-wrought themes.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: A confetti blast of manic female fury. Weird and messy, but a lot of R-rated fun.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: Harley Quinn finally gets her own fun, R-rated, girl power movie and Margot Robbie is exceptionally fierce in the role.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: I like Margot, Rosie, Mary, and Jurnee's Black Canary, I really enjoyed her character a lot.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: Birds of Prey isn't quite great, but it is really good. And REALLY fun. Ultimately, isn't that what you want from a movie like this?
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Birds of Prey... is a fast-paced action movie with fantastic stunts and set pieces. We're just not given any good reason to care about Harley Quinn, or her female compatriots needed to be emotionally invested in their ultimate victory or demise.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: A gleefully over-the-top, candy-colored comic book spectacle that finds a pleasing balance between character and action that puts it a cut above its superhero peers.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: It's angry and incredibly violent and despite its bright color palette - perhaps expectedly dark; it's also cathartic and triumphant.
reviews.author: Carmen Phillips

reviews.text: Margot Robbie is truly a movie star, and Harley Quinn is her signature stroke of charisma. BOP has a weak script, but the colorful action kept me interested for the most part.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: An explosive and campy adventure into the world of DC Comics. Birds of Prey isn't afraid of its wild comic book roots, and reminds you of the colorful pages it comes from.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Birds of Prey follows a familiar formula for other pseudo-anarchic and violent superhero subversions. But what sets this take apart from the Deadpools of the multiplex is its reversal of their toxicity
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: Overall, Birds of Prey is a colorful ball of chaos. Is it a cinematic masterpiece? Far from it. But it's an absolute blast, and that's all it needs to be.
reviews.author: Alexia Amoriello

reviews.text: The type of scrappy mayhem that gives a sparkle of excitement to the mostly bland and boring DCEU.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: A funny, irreverent, extravagant and delightfully violent comic book film that's a blast to witness.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: The film entirely relies on flash, style and suave action, but Margot Robbie's mesmerizing act as Harley Quinn makes this an entertaining watch...
reviews.author: Deborah Cornelious

reviews.text: Mostly, though, the movie works. The set pieces are strong, the action choreography kinetic and fun, and once all the characters are finally in the same place, Birds Of Prey delivers proper super-team mayhem.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Birds of Prey delivers a satisfying action spectacle led by women, but poignancy is the one element missing in the make-up of its addle-brained heroine.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: As proof of concept for Harley Quinn's ability to control center stage, Birds of Prey works...
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Director Cathy Yan and producer/star [Margot] Robbie have brought something fresh, and uniquely feminist to DC's cinematic universe, creating a chaotic yet zesty comics-style spectacle that's exactly the killer escape at the movies it intends to be.
reviews.author: Lina Lecaro

reviews.text: Yan and Robbie and these Birds are able to fly free of the restraints that had been put on them in the past. You might just wish they stop flapping wildly all over the place, crashing into every corner of every wall, ultimately going nowhere in particular
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: The massive plus is that, unlike most of the DCEU, Birds Of Prey offers bountiful bubblegum fun.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: In the end, while Birds of Prey is a step in the right direction for DC in terms of tone and character, it's still a little too jumbled and hectic to truly be a home run.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: A bone-cracking visual feast, filled with screen-popping sets and costumes, enough hand-to-hand combat scenes to make Jason Statham seethe with envy, and a fantastic ensemble cast...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: ...appears to have been made from rotten cotton candy.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Director Cathy Yan and writer Christina Hudson, along with the game Robbie, have crafted a Harley who's daffy but crafty, enraged but never petulant, more exuberant than maniacal.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: But while this definitely has its moments, it's a film that never quite bursts into life, held back by some nasty underlying violence, a story that is simply too complicated and a supporting team that don't quite grasp the opportunity they've been handed.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The humor and zany action throughout the film were on point, and Robbie is clearly having a great time as Harley Quinn, a role she was born to play.
reviews.author: Erik Kain

reviews.text: The momentum steadily fades, though, and that's bad news for a film as shallow as this one.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: This film is one of the boldest in breaking away from overused tropes viewers have come to expect from action and comic book films alike. Women are behaving "badly" in Birds of Prey, and they are extremely unapologetic about it.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a chaotic, violent multi-coloured joy; easily the best of DC's extended universe films to date and the perfect vehicle for its star's inimitable energy.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a blast from start to finish. A celebration of sisterhood and diversity.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: It offers a hundred different versions of Robbie gurning to camera - usually after bashing someone's head in with a baseball bat - and not a single moment to elevate the proceedings above a scrappy, screechy, second-rate cartoon hotchpotch.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Skilful filmmaking elevates this far above the last cinematic outing for Margot Robbie's Harley Quinn... the screenplay touches on issues of female empowerment in ways that are genuinely insightful.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It's passable entertainment on the superhero level, but another opportunity missed to revel in the zany gleeful madness of Harley.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: "Birds of Prey" wants to fly high, powered by its own wild child, rule-breaking spirit. The truth is it never gets off the ground.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: It's a wickedly fun premise and the film's colorful zaniness makes up for its slim story.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Not everything in the film works, but in a post-Justice League cinema environment for the DCEU, Birds of Prey is yet another example that Warner Bros and DC are making interesting choices and expanding their brand in the right way
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: Birds of Prey has ambition and style to spare.
reviews.author: Jack Blackwell

reviews.text: "Birds of Prey" doesn't entirely break new ground, but its attitude and energy are appreciated when it's easy for movies of its kind to be so morose.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: While its narrative can be disjointed at times, Birds of Prey fully leans into its R-rating, making for a hilarious and violent good time
reviews.author: Jay Krieger

reviews.text: The Australian actress Margot Robbie is terribly good as the freaky heroine Harley Quinn.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A consistently humorous comic book flick (although a bit repetitive) and a little longer than it needed to be.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: DC's latest delivers laughs, thrills, oodles of charm, and the best action scenes in a comic book movie since Captain America: The Winter Soldier.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: This is not only the first great movie I've seen this year. This has rocketed up my list of my favorite superhero movies.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Birds of Prey celebrates female empowerment, but it's so much more than the filmmakers' gender; it's a breath of fresh air in a dark and serious superhero space.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: Robbie has this anti-heroine's persona just right, doing disgusting deeds with a big grin. She's even cute! This is one colorful, bad ass female action adventure with an ensemble that will be fun to follow again.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Content to be nihilistic and mean-spirited as an end in itself... it gives the audience not one character it can engage with emotionally or psychologically, leaving them adrift in a world of sensory overload and fetishized violence. In short, it's trash.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: I do wish it did more with the story and explored the characters further, but most of us are here for the Margot Robbie as Harley Quinn show.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: In spite of the formulaic constraints of the male-dominated genre, BIRDS OF PREY soars, swoops, glides, dive-bombs, and sings.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: However, the fight scenes grow tiresome, so does the unnecessary body pile-up. All delivered via ear-debilitating sound mixing. "Birds of Prey" may be R-rated, but the extra gore feels unnecessary here.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: When you understand this distinction, it becomes clear that the women in Birds of Prey dress to please themselves, to increase their fighting efficiency, or to communicate something about who they are.
reviews.author: Meghan White

reviews.text: While it can feel a bit unwieldy as it bounces around willy nilly, the film remains so effortlessly entertaining that it's easy to dismiss such things.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: This group of women who prove they can stand up for themselves makes it a must watch. A really fun movie filled with action & humor. But could have been better.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is like getting smashed in the face with a baseball bat of fun, and its confident madness proves that when DC takes chances, the sky is the limit.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: A hundred times better than I thought it was going to be. Though there were some technical problems, I enjoyed the cast of characters, including, of course, the sarcastic Margot Robbie as Harley Quinn.
reviews.author: Vincent Schilling

reviews.text: Margot Robbie doing backflips in roller-skates...YUP! I'm there for all of it in Birds of Prey and you will be too! Jurnee Smolett, Mary Elizabeth Winstead, Rosie Perez and Ella jay Basco are giving female empowerment a fantabulous, delicious twist!
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: By the end, they each get the chance to prove they shouldn't be underestimated since they're more powerful than the men who kept them down.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: For its ticket price, failed antagonist, and ultimately forgettable emotional arcs, I'd save this one for a plane.
reviews.author: Jordan Calhoun

reviews.text: Of the many things I hate about this origin story, perhaps the thing I hate the most is the way it uses mental illness as a cheap plot device to make Harley's underlying character entirely malleable.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: The toxic male gaze of Suicide Squad is thankfully absent, but the sloppy writing and shoddy filmmaking remain intact.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Harley feels restricted in her own film, an incoherent narrative without any real focus other than a feeble effort to laugh at its own jokes.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: Sort of like Rocky Horror meets a Jackie Chan movie. I'm not sure what to make of it and I kind of appreciate that.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: "Birds of Prey" is filled with busty and implausible action sequences galore, but it does plant a slick pro feminist message in a sea of testosterone infused superhero flicks. Maybe this isn't a man's world after all.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Following Martin Scorsese's criticism of comic book films as theme parks rather than cinema, it's tempting to read Birds of Prey as a satisfyingly minxy comeback: it's the movie equivalent of a fairground ride with all the bolts loosened...
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Birds of Prey make mincemeat of anyone in their way.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: As vibrant and colorful as a pyrotechnic spectacle. Margot Robbie commands this emancipation story with charm, strength and confidence. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Birds of Prey has a shaky start, gets a bit too infatuated with its own kitschy conceits, but when it settles in to the characters quieter stories and the main action, it nails it.
reviews.author: Bill Watters

reviews.text: Harley keeps her ruthless "devil may care" iconic status but she is not in the same movie as the Birds of Prey.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: To put it bluntly, Birds of Prey is a mess, but so is Harley Quinn. How fitting.
reviews.author: Sarah Ksiazek

reviews.text: You don't have to choose between Scorsese and superheroes. Let go of the guilt. Feel free to embrace these lesser spotted birds.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The movie belongs to its outsized performances, the self-aware humor of Hodson's script, costume designer Erin Benach's eye-popping array of fantastical pieces, and cinematographer Matthew Libatique's eye for the playful, colorful, and unconventional.
reviews.author: Melissa Leon

reviews.text: The film strikes oil over and over again, shaping a sharp narrative around a typically chained character and impressively grating a DCEU well that's felt tapped for years.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Robbie... is again fun as this lethal baby-doll, and Perez, Winstead, Basco and Jurnee Smollett-Bell are all strong enough too.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: I enjoyed this wacky, blackly slapstick girls' night out.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: Come for the ass kicking, stay for the takedown of rape culture.
reviews.author: Mary Elizabeth Williams

reviews.text: Superhero movies needed a chaotic anti-heroine, and Margot Robbie ably fills that gap.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: I know it's pointless to review the film they didn't make. But underneath this clangy, pounding, speedy, thin, energetic confetti-shower of a movie is a collection of missed opportunities begging to be noticed.
reviews.author: Johanna Schneller

reviews.text: Ultimately, Birds of Prey ends up being a disappointment, for the moments of explosive, violent fun... are more than cancelled out by its expository stumbles.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: The climax scene where the girls put up a last stand is something you'll remember for its ingenuity.
reviews.author: Devesh Sharma

reviews.text: Thankfully, Birds of Prey never threatens you with a Leto reprisal. Instead, once you get past all the chaos, the Joker's absence actually makes for an interesting premise.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: The title might trumpet Harley Quinn's emancipation, but she again feels like a character trapped in a movie that's mediocre at best.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: In fact it's really good fun. Margot Robbie has great fun with the role.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Better than Deadpool, Birds of Prey delivers the Harley Quinn adventure fans have spent years waiting for and is one of the best DC Comics movies to date.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: Birds of Prey has the spirit of a teenager who wants to be different without admitting that it cares, and the intellectual coefficient of its protagonist. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: Harley Quinn is a fun character trapped in a really bad movie.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Behind the gore and brutality, Birds of Prey is a smart-talking break-up film.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is totally liberated from the garbage that came before it, aiming an eff-you glitter bomb directly at the patriarchy.
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: This movie's woman-first stance is handled well, as the formation of the all-woman hero team feels organic and unforced.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Here are 109 of the most unabashedly enjoyable minutes you'll have at the movies this year.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: "Birds of Prey" serves as a reminder that the "Suicide Squad" concept wasn't wrong; it was just badly done. The new film finds a bit more joy amid the cracking limbs, and a lot more family.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: 'Birds of Prey' is a fast and irreverent spit in the eye to the pomposity of the overblown superhero genre.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: There is certainly fun to be had, but to shoot to fantabulous is going to count as overselling and the liberation most desired will be to escape this fever dream.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Light on superhero effects and heavy on the ass-kicking, Birds of Prey puts its trust in the indomitable Harley Quinn.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: A lower-key DCEU movie is a fine idea. One that commits to Harley's all-out crazy world would be even better.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a divine blend of superheroics and chaotic catharsis, perfectly embodying Harley's titular emancipation from not only The Joker but the past sins of the DCEU.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: There's no Joker in the new Harley Quinn movie, nor in her life, and both are better for it.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: The end result is occasionally entertaining and frequently enervating.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Had Birds of Prey steered just a bit harder into the anarchic, punk rock swagger it occasionally burps with its whiskey-covered breath, it would have fully been the film Robbie deserves.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: But it exults in a vividly hued manic energy that qualifies it for membership of that select category: comic-book movies that actually look and feel like comic books.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Margot Robbie was fun as Harley Quinn in Suicide Squad. Here she is as NOT fun as she was fun it that. It's a supporting character at best & the schtick wears out quickly.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Just like Harley Quinn's persona, Birds of Prey is a chaotic ballet of madness and action where the rules don't apply. It throws caution to the wind and proceeds with reckless abandon.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a celebration of women in their most real and flawed form, badass and unencumbered by the need to impress anyone -- especially men.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: A film that is not nearly and transgressive or anarchistic as it clearly thinks it is, but which still packs enough charm and gleefully brutal go-girl insouciance to make for a reasonably winning entertainment.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Birds of Prey cheapens Robbie's razzle-dazzle characterization by politicizing it; Quinn's personal passion gets reduced to the childish inanity of out-of-control petulance.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Action scenes are first-rate. Robbie delivers remarkably physical performance. There is no plot.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The only time I've not felt talked down to by a comic book movie that purports to be feminist.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: Ultimately, it's a series of fight scenes rather than a story.
reviews.author: John Byrne

reviews.text: Too much is crammed into the first hour and often there is far more style than substance. But the last half hour is perfect and it left me wanting more.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: This is a film that wants so desperately for us to believe it's edgy and twisted that it forgets to actually be edgy and twisted.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: I can finally forget all about Suicide Squad now that we have a proper f*cking Harley Quinn movie. Birds of Prey is a big, sparkly gem of a comic book action movie - and watching Margot Robbie inhabit Harleen Quinzel was pure and absolute joy.
reviews.author: Amie Simon

reviews.text: The parts of Birds of Prey that work are extremely fun, but there's too long of a wait to get there...a disappointment for staying too close to the template.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: I don't really think there was a lot of care given to developing these characters at all throughout the course of this script.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: You don't go to "Birds of Prey" looking for depth of meaning in women's continuing fight for equality with men. You go for bad men being beaten senseless with a bit of style - and a lot of glitter.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Fast, frenetic, colourful and packed with flashbacks and enough momentary diversions to make your head spin...
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: Essentially, "Birds of Prey" wants to be a heroic story. But it fails to embrace - or include - heroic characters.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: Watching it makes me feel like I've been hit with one of those confetti canisters. I could stand being hit again.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: The cinematic equivalent of a super-sized bag of Sweet Tarts. In the hyper-colorized scenes of violence and mayhem, Margot Robbie and her co-stars grab your attention and don't let go.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: In truth, the film directed by Cathy Yan symbolizes better the anti-establishment concept that Todd Phillips' film boasted at the top of its lungs... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: It's a truly mean-spirited piece of work, a nasty ordeal for anyone who cares about characters and why they do what they do. But that doesn't mean it's completely worthless.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Helmed by director Cathy Yan in her first big-budget super-outing, the movie is just too much @#$% fun.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: One of the best aspects of Birds of Prey is its extreme levity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: Robbie's outlandish performance still dominates; she's like Lucille Ball plopped into a Spandex nightmare, mugging and wise-cracking her way through the chaos. Even when the movie loses focus, she stays razor-sharp.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Purposely untidy and at times cheerfully off-putting, Birds is more memorably unhinged than the likes of Joker, Venom, and Deadpool.
reviews.author: Christopher Schobert

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is fun as hell. Kinetic, comedic, self-aware, and with just the right amount of R-rated brutality and grit.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: In a weird way, it's the first comic book film that feels punk rock.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Cathy Yan's film felt like a colorful piñata exploding sprinkles of awesomeness right before my eyes.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: Margot Robbie is unstoppable as Harley Quinn, but the screenplay fails this DC Comics adaptation.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: [T]he point here is ass-kicking sisterhood with comic flourishes that land with varying degrees of success.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: [Has] a contemporary verve that offers a glimpse of something heartening: a future in which all kinds of people get to tell these stories, and we're all the better off for it.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Birds Of Prey is a huge, neon-tinged, nihilistic pack of fun - for those of the right age. Those films about boys in capes could learn a lot from this.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: ...[Yan]'s written her own ticket here, confidently managing the shifting tones between each character's subplot and proving as adept at framing action as she is at mixing charming comedy with some truly discomforting horror elements.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Birds of Prey may not have the depth and darkness of the recent Joker but it is a fun popcorn flick.
reviews.author: S. Indra Sathiabalan

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a brutally satisifying and intoxicatingly vibrant explosion of fun. A film made by women for women about women, but operates in a capacity that is enjoyable for everyone.
reviews.author: Amanda Sink

reviews.text: By letting action and comedy become augmentation for its underlying crime caper, it proves more character-driven romp a la Snatch than another ploddingly edgelord blockbuster.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: There's a pervasive air of desperation to this female-centric would-be comic-book action blockbuster, which flails about for nearly two hours trying to be edgy and snarky in 'Deadpool' mode but fails miserably on all counts.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Perhaps the greatest sign of female empowerment is that they can now fight, curse, maim, and kill as well as the boys do onscreen. I'm not sure what that says about our society, but it sure makes for some nasty fun at the Cineplex.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: A schizophrenic, barely comprehensible spinoff. It turns out Harley Quinn is entertaining only in small doses.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: As the opening installment of a projected franchise, it's pretty promising...
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Margot Robbie's Harley Quinn epic is not as gargantuanly godawful as Suicde Squad, but slapping the topical theme of female empowerment on a story that trucks in business-as-usual blood-and-guts does not qualify as a game-changer.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: An unholy and sadistic mess.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Birds of Prey may not amount to anything truly game-changing but it's still top-tier comic book stuff.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: A lean, tightly choreographed film, with gorgeous fight scenes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: I came in hoping this would be a triumphant all-girl, kick-ass, riotous action movie. In the end I found it to be unfocused, derivative, loud, obnoxious, and actually kinda boring.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Combining all the ingredients that make comic book bros break out in hives, Birds of Prey is a candy-coloured curveball of a movie that doubles as a feminist fable and an apology for the poorly received Suicide Squad.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: A psychedelic piñata filled with more sweet than bitter things . [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Birds of Prey has all of the chaotic energy that a movie about Harley Quinn should have packaged in a frenetic action-filled romp that's impossible to resist. The best DCEU movie yet.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Comes across as a crudely stitched together collection of studio-approved scenes. Quinn's inherent chaos is turned into bubblegum, and the flavor runs out quickly.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Birds of Prey isn't perfect, but it sure is fantabulous, and that's because Harley finally landed in the right hands: her own.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: The wacky, nearly too-cute action-comedy is crammed with scattershot efforts meant to entertain at all costs. Its story makes no sense, the narrative flow is disconnected and there's little plot and even less payoff.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Violent and profane, but themes of teamwork, friendship.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Birds of Prey allows Robbie to truly let loose, giving her the space to develop an actual character beyond the one-dimensional, sociopathic quip machine that she was in Suicide Squad.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Led by a cutesy head-butt of a performance from superstar Margo Robbie, 'Birds of Prey' is a do-over of sorts for the much-maligned Suicide Squad.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The result is a slapstick firework display of pleasantly cartoonish mayhem.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Birds of Prey puts the audience in the shoes (or roller skates) or somebody who gets a perverse thrill from nihilistic violence. Like it or not, it's a rush.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: It's too bad that things devolve into the ordinary by the last act, but until that happens, we zig and zag in often pleasant ways.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Perhaps not as fun as it wants to be, but the movie has high spirits and a refreshing perspective that goes a bit deeper than just grrrl power.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: At its core, Birds of Prey is not just a film to wipe the slate clean for the Crown Princess of Crime, but to establish that the toxicity present, the male-domination that creeps through [Suicide] Squad, is a thing of the past.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The film is a triumph of female-led filmmaking...[but] it's squarely mid-level DC, and while I'm glad it emancipated Harley Quinn, I'm already eager to move on and see what she gets up to next.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The new DC superhero film has some pop and flash, but too often feels like a bunch of different plotlines smashed together.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: The ensuing girls-versus-bad-men melee works as a satisfyingly noisy outlet for the movie's female rage, but Yan and Hodson also take time to sketch out moments of sisterhood that give the mayhem some form of emotional anchor.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Fantabulous is a bit of an overstatement for the sassy shenanigans in DC Comics' Birds of Prey, but this spunky vehicle for the breakout star of Suicide Squad is remarkably honest about its own limitations.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Much of this R-rated movie is chaotic, yet it's a richly hued, madly inventive, gleefully violent and happily slapdash contraption with a formidable female at its center.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: It's a collage of glitter-packed fun.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: For a movie that touts its protagonist's emancipation, Birds of Prey still feels very much in chains.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: Birds of Prey may be a manic circus, but it proves to be the best kind of circus - one without a clown.
reviews.author: Glen Weldon

reviews.text: Birds of Prey is a glorious, hyperkinetic mess and, although it never quite takes flight, it at least holds the attention.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

synopsis: It's open season on Harley Quinn when her explosive breakup with the Joker puts a big fat target on her back. Unprotected and on the run, Quinn faces the wrath of narcissistic crime boss Black Mask, his right-hand man, Victor Zsasz, and every other thug in the city. But things soon even out for Harley when she becomes unexpected allies with three deadly women -- Huntress, Black Canary and Renee Montoya.
